title: Victim's friends seeking reform
article: Family and friends of Deng Fermino Kuol -- shot dead early Saturday by a Calgary police officer he stabbed -- are demanding police explain why the officer shot to kill.
The incident has also prompted Stephen Jenuth, president of the Alberta Civil Liberties Association, to call for the creation of an independent body to investigate such incidents.

"The situation we have now ... makes it very unlikely that police misconduct ever gets found," Jenuth said. "And with the cases where it is found, it has to be so egregious that it just can't go unpunished."
Akwoch Ding, a friend of Kuol's for the past five years, is calling for the provincial government to intervene in the investigation and to change the way police handle such situations.
"We are really very sad and we feel like something has to be done by the government. The police has to be reformed," Ding said.
Kuol's cousin, Akon Malou, said the "police have a lot of things to use" in subduing attackers, pointing to batons and pepper spray as examples.
Piot Dol, a friend of Kuol's, added that if the officer was finding it hard to get Kuol's co-operation in leaving the building, he should have called for backup.
Const. Ira Macumber responded to a call to remove Kuol, 34, from a basement suite early Saturday.
Kuol, who was unemployed and homeless after being laid off from Lakeside Packers in Brooks earlier this year, was sitting outside the apartment when Macumber arrived.
Investigators said after initially agreeing to go with Macumber, Kuol drew a knife and slashed the officer in the left bicep.
Macumber struggled to restrain his attacker and then pulled his gun, firing twice -- in keeping with police training.
Kuol's family and friends gathered Sunday afternoon in southeast Calgary to console each other.
Kuol was attempting to sponsor his two sisters in Kenya to immigrate to Canada, Malou said.
Bol Agot, 24, described his brother as an "honest" person who had many friends and enjoyed talking to people.
Homicide investigators are now trying to determine if Macumber was justified in using deadly force to subdue Kuol.

Once the homicide unit's investigation is done, the findings will be reviewed by the Calgary police professional standards section for possible disciplinary action and by the Crown prosecutor's office for any possible criminal charges.
